```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
set.seed(2026)
# non-ASCII characters in output and plots under a "C" locale
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(fmt(100 * x, d), "%")
```

An aeroplane has two engines, a server two power supplies, a hospital a generator for power cuts. The idea is always the same: components fail, but a system can be designed to **keep working**. How reliable is it? With the rules for [independent events](../independence/index.qmd) we can compute it.

## Reliability

The **reliability** of a component is the probability $p$ that it works properly over a given period, say one year. In this post we assume that components fail **independently** of each other.

## In series: all are needed

In a **series** layout the system works only if **all** components work, like the bulbs of an old string of fairy lights. By independence:

$$R_{\text{series}} = p_1 \cdot p_2 \cdots p_n.$$

A machine needs three components with reliability 0.95, 0.90 and 0.92. Its reliability is $0.95 \cdot 0.90 \cdot 0.92 = 0.7866$, so it fails within the year with probability $0.2134$, as we found in the independence post.

The product shrinks fast. A system of 100 components in series, each with 99% reliability, works all year with probability only $0.99^{100} \approx$ `r fmt(0.99^100, 3)`.

## In parallel: one is enough

In a **parallel** layout the system works if **at least one** component works. It is easier to compute the complement: the system fails only if all components fail.

$$R_{\text{parallel}} = 1 - (1 - p_1)(1 - p_2) \cdots (1 - p_n).$$

Two sensors with reliability 0.9 each, in parallel, give $1 - 0.1^2 = 0.99$. **Redundancy** cuts the probability of failure from 10% to 1%.

## Mixed systems and "2 out of 3"

Real systems combine the two. We compute them from the inside out, replacing each subsystem by its reliability. For example, $A$ in series with $B$ and $C$ in parallel:

$$R = p_A \cdot \big[1 - (1 - p_B)(1 - p_C)\big].$$

Another common layout is **"2 out of 3"**: the system works if at least two of three components work, as with three independent instruments that "vote" on an aircraft. If all three have reliability $p$, by [combinations](../combinations/index.qmd):

$$R_{2/3} = \binom{3}{2} p^2 (1 - p) + \binom{3}{3} p^3 = 3p^2 - 2p^3.$$

Choose a layout and reliabilities in the diagram, and simulate a year of operation:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof st30 = Inputs.select(new Map([
  ["Three in series", "series"], ["Three in parallel", "parallel"],
  ["A in series with (B ∥ C)", "mixed1"], ["(A – B) ∥ C", "mixed2"], ["2 out of 3", "vote"]
]), {label: "Layout"})
viewof p30 = Inputs.form([
  Inputs.range([0.5, 1], {label: "Reliability of A", step: 0.01, value: 0.9}),
  Inputs.range([0.5, 1], {label: "Reliability of B", step: 0.01, value: 0.8}),
  Inputs.range([0.5, 1], {label: "Reliability of C", step: 0.01, value: 0.85})
])
viewof sim30 = Inputs.button("Simulate one year")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  sim30;
  const [a, b, c] = p30;
  const works = (A, B, C) => ({series: A && B && C, parallel: A || B || C, mixed1: A && (B || C), mixed2: (A && B) || C, vote: (A + B + C) >= 2})[st30];
  const exact = ({series: a * b * c, parallel: 1 - (1 - a) * (1 - b) * (1 - c), mixed1: a * (1 - (1 - b) * (1 - c)), mixed2: 1 - (1 - a * b) * (1 - c),
    vote: a * b * (1 - c) + a * (1 - b) * c + (1 - a) * b * c + a * b * c})[st30];
  const s = sim30 > 0 ? [Math.random() < a, Math.random() < b, Math.random() < c] : [true, true, true];
  let k = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) if (works(Math.random() < a, Math.random() < b, Math.random() < c)) k++;
  // box positions for each layout
  const L = {series: [[60, 70], [170, 70], [280, 70]], parallel: [[170, 20], [170, 70], [170, 120]], mixed1: [[80, 70], [240, 35], [240, 105]],
    mixed2: [[120, 40], [230, 40], [175, 110]], vote: [[170, 20], [170, 70], [170, 120]]}[st30];
  const W = 380, H = 150, bw = 64, bh = 30, names = ["A", "B", "C"];
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", W + "px").style("font", "14px sans-serif");
  const line = (x1, y1, x2, y2) => svg.append("path").attr("d", `M${x1},${y1}L${x2},${y2}`).attr("stroke", "#888").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("fill", "none");
  const inL = 10, outR = W - 10, mid = 70;
  const left = ([x, y]) => [x - bw / 2, y], right = ([x, y]) => [x + bw / 2, y];
  const toBus = (p, xb) => { line(xb, p[1], p[0], p[1]); };
  if (st30 === "series") { line(inL, mid, left(L[0])[0], mid); line(right(L[0])[0], mid, left(L[1])[0], mid); line(right(L[1])[0], mid, left(L[2])[0], mid); line(right(L[2])[0], mid, outR, mid); }
  else if (st30 === "parallel" || st30 === "vote") { const xl = 90, xr = 250; line(inL, mid, xl, mid); line(xr, mid, outR, mid); line(xl, 20, xl, 120); line(xr, 20, xr, 120); L.forEach(p => { toBus(left(p), xl); line(right(p)[0], p[1], xr, p[1]); }); }
  else if (st30 === "mixed1") { const xl = 175, xr = 305; line(inL, mid, left(L[0])[0], mid); line(right(L[0])[0], mid, xl, mid); line(xl, 35, xl, 105); line(xr, 35, xr, 105); line(xr, mid, outR, mid); [L[1], L[2]].forEach(p => { toBus(left(p), xl); line(right(p)[0], p[1], xr, p[1]); }); }
  else { const xl = 50, xr = 300; line(inL, mid, xl, mid); line(xr, mid, outR, mid); line(xl, 40, xl, 110); line(xr, 40, xr, 110); line(xl, 40, left(L[0])[0], 40); line(right(L[0])[0], 40, left(L[1])[0], 40); line(right(L[1])[0], 40, xr, 40); line(xl, 110, left(L[2])[0], 110); line(right(L[2])[0], 110, xr, 110); }
  L.forEach(([x, y], i) => {
    svg.append("rect").attr("x", x - bw / 2).attr("y", y - bh / 2).attr("width", bw).attr("height", bh).attr("rx", 6)
      .attr("fill", s[i] ? "#e8f5e9" : "#fdecea").attr("stroke", s[i] ? "#2e7d32" : "#c62828").attr("stroke-width", 2);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", x).attr("y", y).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "middle").text(`${names[i]} ${s[i] ? "✓" : "✗"}`);
  });
  if (st30 === "vote") svg.append("text").attr("x", 300).attr("y", 18).attr("fill", "#4e79a7").text("≥ 2 of 3");
  const ok = works(...s);
  const f = x => x.toLocaleString("en-GB", {minimumFractionDigits: 4, maximumFractionDigits: 4});
  return html`${svg.node()}
    <div class="ix-note">${sim30 > 0 ? html`This year the system <b style="color:${ok ? "#2e7d32" : "#c62828"}">${ok ? "worked" : "failed"}</b>.` : html`Press "Simulate one year" to see which components fail.`}</div>
    <table class="ix-tbl">
      <tr><td>System reliability (exact)</td><td><b>${f(exact)}</b></td></tr>
      <tr><td>Frequency over 10,000 years</td><td><b>${f(k / 10000)}</b></td></tr>
      <tr><td>Most reliable component alone</td><td><b>${f(Math.max(a, b, c))}</b></td></tr>
    </table>`;
}
```
:::

Compare the last row of the table with the first. In series the system is **less** reliable than its weakest component. In parallel it is **more** reliable than its best one.

## In R

```{r}
#| label: reliability-r
series <- function(p) prod(p)
parallel <- function(p) 1 - prod(1 - p)
p <- c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8, C = 0.85)
c(series = series(p), parallel = parallel(p),
  mixed1 = p[["A"]] * parallel(p[c("B", "C")]),
  mixed2 = parallel(c(series(p[c("A", "B")]), p[["C"]])))
# simulation of A in series with (B || C)
up <- matrix(runif(3 * 100000) < p, nrow = 3)
mean(up[1, ] & (up[2, ] | up[3, ]))
```

In the simulation the matrix `up` has one column per "year" and one row per component. R recycles the vector `p` down the rows, so each component gets its own reliability.

## An important assumption

All the formulas rest on **independent** failures. In practice there are **common-cause failures**: a fire, a surge on the power grid or a software bug can hit all the redundant components at once. Then the parallel layout protects much less than the formula promises. That is why engineers aim for redundancy with **different** components, in different places.

## Key takeaways

- **In series:** $R = \prod p_i$. The system is less reliable than its weakest component.
- **In parallel:** $R = 1 - \prod (1 - p_i)$. Redundancy cuts the probability of failure dramatically.
- Mixed systems are computed from the inside out. "2 out of 3" needs combinations.
- Everything assumes independent failures. Common-cause failures change the picture.

## Review questions

**1. Quick quiz.**

::: {.ix-panel}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz30 = [
  {q: "Two components with reliability 0.9 in series. What is the system's reliability?",
   opts: ["0.99", "0.9", "0.81", "0.18"], ans: 2,
   why: "In series both are needed: 0.9 · 0.9 = 0.81."},
  {q: "The same two components in parallel?",
   opts: ["0.99", "0.9", "0.81", "1"], ans: 0,
   why: "It fails only if both fail: 1 − 0.1 · 0.1 = 0.99."},
  {q: "How many components with reliability 0.8 are needed in parallel for the reliability to exceed 0.999?",
   opts: ["3", "4", "5", "10"], ans: 2,
   why: "1 − 0.2ⁿ > 0.999 ⇔ 0.2ⁿ < 0.001. Now 0.2⁴ = 0.0016 and 0.2⁵ = 0.00032, so n = 5."},
  {q: "Three components with reliability 0.9 in a 2-out-of-3 layout. What is the reliability?",
   opts: ["0.729", "0.972", "0.999", "0.9"], ans: 1,
   why: "3p² − 2p³ = 3 · 0.81 − 2 · 0.729 = 2.43 − 1.458 = 0.972."}
]
{
  const root = html`<div></div>`, score = html`<div class="ix-note"></div>`, done = new Map();
  quiz30.forEach((item, k) => {
    const fb = html`<div class="ix-note"></div>`;
    const btns = item.opts.map(o => html`<button>${o}</button>`);
    const opts = html`<div style="margin:4px 0 0 6px">${btns.map((b, j) => {
      b.onclick = () => {
        const ok = j === item.ans; done.set(k, ok);
        btns.forEach(x => x.className = "");
        b.className = ok ? "ix-picked-ok" : "ix-picked-no";
        fb.innerHTML = (ok ? `<span class="ix-ok">✓ Correct.</span> ` : `<span class="ix-no">✗ Not quite.</span> `) + item.why;
        score.innerHTML = `<b>Correct: ${[...done.values()].filter(x => x).length} of ${quiz30.length}</b>`;
      };
      return b;
    })}</div>`;
    root.append(html`<div style="margin:12px 0"><div>${k + 1}. ${item.q}</div>${opts}${fb}</div>`);
  });
  root.append(score);
  return root;
}
```
:::

**2.** A system has two branches in parallel. Each branch is two components in series, all with reliability $p$. Find its reliability. Is it better than a system of two parallel pairs in series, $(A \parallel B) - (C \parallel D)$?

**3.** For which values of $p$ is "2 out of 3" more reliable than a single component?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answers

2. Series branches in parallel: $R_1 = 1 - (1 - p^2)^2$. Parallel pairs in series: $R_2 = \big[1 - (1 - p)^2\big]^2$. For every $0 < p < 1$, $R_2 > R_1$; for example with $p = 0.9$: $R_1 =$ `r fmt(1 - (1 - 0.81)^2, 4)` and $R_2 =$ `r fmt((1 - 0.01)^2, 4)`. Redundancy at the component level beats redundancy at the branch level.
3. $3p^2 - 2p^3 > p \iff p(1 - p)(2p - 1) > 0 \iff p > 1/2$. If the components are unreliable ($p < 1/2$), "voting" makes things worse.
:::
